There was some rain, and at least half the people in line had umbrellas. Everywhere I looked I saw Q shirts, hats and signs. Given the way the line was formed, I was able to observe hundreds upon hundreds of people as we snaked along. If I had to estimate the percentage with Q attire, it would be up to 5%. I bet at least five times their number know about Q but lacked a visible indicator of that awareness. I heard WWG1WGA chants all through the crowd.

The venue -- a sports arena -- confiscated all the umbrellas on the way in. Everyone was searched and passed through metal detectors. They wanted D. who went with me to throw his Swiss army knife in the trash, but I took that and our umbrellas and stashed them outside next to a concrete planter. (All three items were still there when we came out.)

The building seats 11,000 people with room for another 1,200 or so to stand up on the floor of the arena (the actual basketball court). We got in around 3:00 p.m. and it was almost half full at that point. They had opened the doors early because of the rain and started letting people in around 2:00. By 6:00 there wasn't an empty seat left (except right behind the cameras and stuff at the end of the arena), the floor was packed, and several thousand more people had been turned away. It's amazing to see a place that big filled to the rafters. I haven't seen anything like it since the first Beatles concert at Olympia Stadium in Detroit in 1964.

The speakers started off with a former pastor from Branson doing a prayer/invocation, then the pledge of allegiance and national anthem. Then US Rep. Billy Long (MO-7) came out and spoke for about ten minutes. Then Rep. Jason Smith (MO-8, my district) spoke for ten minutes or so. Then Josh Hawley's wife spoke for a while. Then there was an interval of music before Trump came out.

I had left my seat around 5:30 and went down on the arena floor. (D. stayed in the stands.) I gradually slipped closer and closer to the stage until finally by the time Trump came out, I was about 15' from the podium. I wanted to observe him from as near as possible at least for a short time.

While I was on the floor, something happened that I didn't expect. Trump stood off to the side while Hawley spoke. At that point Trump was about 12' from me. He would look at Hawley for a few moments, then look into the crowd and wink, wave or gesture to someone, then look back at Hawley, etc. About five minutes into Hawley's speech, Trump looked at someone standing near me, off to my right a bit and slightly behind me. He pointed at them, then drew the letter Q with his hand, three times in succession, very quickly!

Anyone not in or very close to the line of sight of Trump's pointing finger would only have seen the finger moving and missed the motion of his hand clearly drawing a circle then slicing through it with the angled straight line near the bottom. Everyone around me was recording the event, so I'm sure someone captured it. I hope someone who follows Q recorded it and will post a clip somewhere.

Right after it happened, I turned my head to see who Trump had been signaling to, but bodies blocked my view. I did catch the eye of a woman whose face was showing the amazement that I was feeling. We had a bit of eye-to-eye communication that said "Hey, did you catch that? He made three Q's in the air!"

I stayed on the floor through the first half of Trump's speech, then I had to go to the restroom. Then I wasn't allowed to go back down onto the floor, so I rejoined D. in the seats. We were about six times farther from the stage than I had been when I was down on the floor, but we still had a clear view.
